messages.subject: mlogit
messages.body_plain:
I'm having trouble getting Zelig to run simulations from a multinomial
logit model.  The DV is called "defhow2" and has five categories, and
I'm running the following syntax:

 

ppicjan10 <- read.dta("Jan 2010.regonly.dta", convert.factors=FALSE)

ppicjan10$defhow2 <- factor(ppicjan10$defhow2, levels=c(1,2,3,4,8),
labels=c("cuts", "taxes",

                "cuts+taxes", "borrow", "other/dk"))

z.out <- zelig(as.factor(defhow2) ~
age+income+educ+lat+sex2+own2+cv+ba+osc+oth+pid7+ideo5+

 
ageXginfo+incXginfo+educXginfo+latXginfo+ownXginfo+cvXginfo+baXginfo+osc
Xginfo+

                othXginfo+pidXginfo+ideoXginfo+ginfo, model="mlogit",
data=ppicjan10, baseline="other/dk")

x.out <- setx(z.out, fn=NULL)

s.out <- sim(z.out, x=x.out)

 

Everything is fine until the simulation command, where I get the
following error:

 

Error in factor(pr, levels = sort(unique(pr)), labels = ynames) : 

  invalid labels; length 5 should be 1 or 4

 

Resources online suggest that missing data is often to blame for this
error message, so I eliminated all of my missing data just to see if I
could get it to work in principle.  No luck-same message.  Does anyone
know what might be going on?

levels (a defined value, but no values of that defined value), but

list-wise deletion before, then check to see how many levels are
actually left in defhow2, then do factor(...) as you have it below
with those levels only.

Yours,

its probably collinearity.  run a regression; if that works (with all
the variables included), the mlogit will usually work.

stats runs anything but it does that by dropping variables.  so unless
you're watching closely, you wind up estimating a model you didn't ask
it to run.

Gary

messages.body_plain:
for logit, there are only 2 things that can cause it to fail:
collinearity and perfect discrimination.

you're using mlogit, and so you can add to that that each of these can
be true for any of the individual equations.  If you have very rare
events in one of them, this can happen easily.
Gary

messages.body_plain:
If your dataset is very large, this could be a problem with Zelig.
However, if your data are relatively small (under a million
observations), then the problem probably isn't Zelig, but is probably
everything else that you have in your R workspace (which also eats up
memory, even if you're not using those objects at the moment).

Tips for freeing memory:

Try quitting R (don't save the workspace) and restarting the session.

If you don't want to quit, remove() extra data objects from the
workspace that you don't need.  For example, if you cleaned your data
and created several versions of the data set, remove everything except
for my.data -- then type
  gc()

Yours,
Olivia
